nuggets.title: Uncoordinated Workers Trigger Publisher IP Ban

scenario.symptoms: Major news site returns HTTP 403 for all crawler IPs. Rate limit logs show 40 concurrent connections to one host during sitemap burst.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Global URL queue allows any worker to fetch any host; per-host delay stored in local memory only.

incident.headline: Global frontier without per-host ownership violates politeness and triggers site-wide block

agenda.goal: Design a frontier that guarantees politeness (single worker ownership per host) and handles priorities.
agenda.opener: We got banned because dozens of workers hammered one site at once. How do you ensure polite crawling at scale?

evidence.strong: Partition frontier by host hash with one owner, per-host back-queue enforcing delay, respect robots crawl-delay, central politeness state.
evidence.weak: Global queue with hope for randomness.

misconceptions.pattern: A single global Kafka topic or RabbitMQ queue can easily handle the frontier.
misconceptions.challenge: If 10 URLs for the same host are pulled by 10 different workers at the exact same time, how do you prevent hitting the host 10 times concurrently?

probes: Walk me through the lifecycle of a URL from the frontier to the worker.
How do we handle a scenario where two different hostnames resolve to the same underlying IP address?
hints: If any worker can pull any URL at random, enforcing global rate limits is very difficult.
What if all URLs belonging to a specific host were always routed to the exact same worker?
agenda.referenceFix: Partitioned frontier by host hash with politeness back-queues.

nuggets.title: Database Lookup Per URL Crawl Grinds Throughput to a Halt

scenario.symptoms: Crawl rate drops from 40k pages/sec to 2k after dedupe moved to Postgres primary. CPU on DB cluster saturates on SELECT by URL hash.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Every discovered link triggers point lookup in relational DB; no Bloom filter or normalization before check.

incident.headline: Synchronous database dedupe becomes bottleneck at billion-URL crawl scale

agenda.goal: Efficiently check if a URL has been crawled before without exhausting memory or database I/O.
agenda.opener: Dedupe lookups crushed our database and crawl speed fell 20x. How do you check if a URL was already crawled?

evidence.strong: Bloom filter in memory with KV backing store, canonical URL normalization before hash, batch existence checks, sharded dedupe store.
evidence.adequate: Redis set of all URLs without Bloom.

misconceptions.pattern: Just query the database to see if the URL exists.
misconceptions.challenge: At 100,000 URLs discovered per second, can a standard relational database handle that many point reads?

probes: How much memory would storing a billion raw URLs take?
What happens if two functionally identical URLs have different tracking query parameters?
hints: Is there a data structure that trades a tiny false positive rate for massive memory savings?
Before we hash a URL to check it, should 'example.com/' and 'example.com' be treated as different pages?
agenda.referenceFix: Bloom filter for fast seen-URL checks with URL normalisation.

nuggets.title: Mirror Sites Fill Storage with Near-Duplicate Pages

scenario.symptoms: Object storage costs jump 3x in a quarter; 60% of bytes are near-identical syndicated articles at different URLs.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Crawler stores every 200 OK body keyed by URL without Simhash or checksum dedupe across content.

incident.headline: URL-only identity stores duplicate and near-duplicate content repeatedly

agenda.goal: Identify and discard duplicate or near-duplicate content across completely different URLs.
agenda.opener: Storage costs exploded because we keep the same article from dozens of URLs. How do you dedupe content, not just URLs?

evidence.strong: Simhash or MinHash for near-dupe, SHA for exact, store canonical copy with aliases, skip indexing duplicates.

probes: How do you detect when a news article is exactly the same, but has a different timestamp or ad banner?
Where are these content hashes stored and queried during the pipeline?
hints: Can we generate a fingerprint of the text that stays similar if the text is mostly the same?
What happens to a standard MD5 hash if a single character in the HTML changes?
agenda.referenceFix: Simhash or standard checksums for content deduplication.

nuggets.title: Central DNS Resolver Becomes Crawl Throughput Ceiling

scenario.symptoms: Fetcher CPU idle at 30% while crawl QPS flatlines. Profiles show 70% of worker time blocked on getaddrinfo to corporate DNS.
scenario.interviewerSetup: All workers use shared corporate resolver without local cache; high unique domain churn on web crawl.

incident.headline: Uncached DNS lookups dominate fetch latency and cap distributed crawler throughput

agenda.goal: Prevent DNS resolution from becoming a silent bottleneck for the fetchers.
agenda.opener: Workers sit idle waiting on DNS while crawl QPS flatlines. How does your crawler handle millions of domain lookups?

evidence.strong: Local caching resolver on each worker with TTL respect, prefetch hot domains, async DNS library, monitor cache hit rate.
evidence.adequate: Central Redis DNS cache with network hop.

probes: What happens if a domain's IP changes frequently due to round-robin load balancing?
Where exactly does the DNS cache live in your architecture?
hints: If every HTTP request requires a round trip to an external DNS server, what happens to our latency?
Can we cache IP addresses locally on the fetcher machines themselves?
agenda.referenceFix: Local DNS caching on fetcher nodes.

nuggets.title: Crashed Worker Leaves URLs Stuck In-Flight Forever

scenario.symptoms: After spot instance reclaim, 2M URLs never finish crawling. Frontier marks them IN_PROGRESS with no lease expiry.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Workers ACK URL batches only after full processing; no visibility timeout or heartbeats on claimed work.

incident.headline: Missing lease recovery leaves frontier URLs permanently in-flight after worker failure

agenda.goal: Ensure the crawler can recover from worker crashes without losing the frontier state or getting stuck.
agenda.opener: Spot kills left millions of URLs stuck in progress. What happens to in-flight URLs when a worker dies?

evidence.strong: Visibility timeout on queue claims, heartbeats extend lease, checkpoint frontier to durable store, idempotent fetch processing, automatic requeue.
evidence.adequate: Manual SQL reset of stuck rows.

probes: How does the frontier definitively know a worker actually finished fetching a URL?
Where is the massive state of the frontier saved if the whole data center restarts?
hints: If a worker pulls a URL, what happens if it unplugs from the wall before finishing the fetch?
Think about how message queues handle unacknowledged messages.
agenda.referenceFix: Visibility timeouts and persistent frontier checkpointing.
